answer_1.quote: We use different instruction-tuned LLMs to create text pairs where the generated texts exhibit either more or less persuasive language than the original ones.
answer_1.outputs: paraphrased texts with more or less persuasive language

answer_2.quote: We fine-tune a regression model on the pairwise data using the pre-trained DebertaV3-Large model using a Mean Square Error Loss.

answer_4.quote: We obtain annotations through crowdsourcing of the persuasive pairs by using three annotators for each text pair on multiple batches. We recruit annotators through the Prolific platform.
answer_4.guideline: We present annotators with pairs of short texts and ask which of the two uses more persuasive language and by how much more, indicated by the following scale: • Marginally more: "If I have to choose, I would lean toward the selected one to be a bit more persuasive." • Moderately More: "I think the selected one is using some more persuasive language." • Heavily More: "The selected one uses a lot more persuasive language, and I can clearly point to why I think it is a lot more."
